rationale: Interpreted the successor receipt d80cbfd9f9a547639811aeacb19c0a30 (fixed experiment d9390caf51ee413aaf05a733db9b99ff-experiment, comparison 0 violated with witness 25): the executor's retry completes the recovered NOOP commit while a live replica keeps the committed value X, so the value-adoption account's earlier counterevidence item that recorded 'no completed contradiction' is withdrawn and replaced by the measured statement; the status-guard account now records the stall as per-attempt and its measured retry outcome.

knowledge.statement: In handlePreAcceptReply the block at epaxos/epaxos.go:876-881 overwrites lb.ballot, lb.cmds, lb.status, lb.seq and lb.deps whenever a reply's VBallot is >= the running lb.ballot, so a reply whose Status is COMMITTED replaces lb.status with COMMITTED; the guard immediately before it (epaxos/epaxos.go:870) returns for any reply while lb.status is neither PREACCEPTED nor PREACCEPTED_EQ, so every later reply to the same PreAccept is discarded and lb.preAcceptOKs stops increasing, leaving the leader's proposal in the pre-accept state for that attempt. A later attempt is not blocked the same way because the coordinator's own value-ballot token then equals the tried ballot, so the reply is no longer adopted and is counted toward the quorum instead.
knowledge.conditions: A phase-1 proposal whose acceptor set includes a replica that already has the instance COMMITTED (or a recoverer that adopted such a status), as happens when a recovery is restarted from sub-case 6 by a replica that lacks the value while another replica has it committed (epaxos/epaxos.go:847-895, 1236-1313).

interpretations.rationale: Current account: a recovery driven by a replica that does not itself hold the command replaces the value carried by its prepare replies with a NOOP, and the replacement is now executed to a completed contradiction of a value another live replica has committed. Witnesses: (1) receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 (fixed experiment fc825b4d2a9c488e8c03dff32b05cab7-experiment) - the accepted value X at ballot 0 is replaced, the self reply's fabricated VBallot 8 shadows the genuine reply at value ballot 0, sub-case 6 selects startPhase1 with state.NOOP() and the holder loses X (comparison 1 violated, witness 20). (2) Receipt d80cbfd9f9a547639811aeacb19c0a30 (successor fixed experiment d9390caf51ee413aaf05a733db9b99ff-experiment, test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoveryContradictsCommittedValue, 30 parsed events, no parsing errors): the owner commits X (index 6, status COMMITTED, cmd_op 1) and its Commit reaches only replica 2 (index 10), so replica 2 holds instance (0,0) COMMITTED with X (index 11, also index 26 at the end); replica 3, which holds no command, then recovers the instance, its prepare reply from replica 2 reports X with Status COMMITTED at value ballot 0 (index 16), yet the recovery emits a PreAccept carrying the NOOP (index 19, comparison 0 of that experiment violated with witness 25 of the final state). The first recovery attempt stalls (index 21: replica 3 PREACCEPTED), and the executor's retry dispatches (index 24: three appended replies, instance status ACCEPTED) and commits the NOOP at replicas 3 and 4 (indices 25 and 27: COMMITTED with cmd_op 0) while replica 2 still holds X committed (index 26) - two live replicas therefore hold different decided values for the same instance (0,0), which is the agreement violation this question's mechanism produces. The mechanism remains the fabricated self value ballot: startRecoveryForInstance sets lb.ballot to the pre-recovery local vbal and then overwrites inst.vbal with the freshly tried ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1145, 1150-1153), so the self reply's VBallot outranks the genuine reply at value ballot 0 and the adoption loop at epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246 keeps lb.cmds nil and lb.status NONE.
counterevidence: The defect is bounded to coordinators that lack the command, and that bound is executed: control experiment 242eaa8afa384a87b0952fbcd4b074b4-experiment (receipt 9d07449105684a498113db891da025d9) replayed the value-adoption crash pattern with the recovery driven by replica 2, which holds X; its preservation comparisons hold, evaluating indices 17 and 19-20.

Event 16 of receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 shows the adoption is a ballot ordering, not a general discard: a reply whose value ballot exceeded the coordinator's own recovery ballot would still be adopted.

The committed peer is protected in its own state: replica 2 ignores the recovered PreAccept and the recovered Commit because its instance is already COMMITTED (epaxos/epaxos.go:1082 and the Cmds-nil branch of epaxos/epaxos.go:807), so the contradiction is between two replicas' decided values rather than a silent rewrite at the holder.

The countervailing ballot-climb path in makeBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451) is gated on IsLeader, which is false in all these executions and in epaxos.New; the master-designated leader's behaviour was excluded from the scopes.
limitations: One configuration and one instance in all three receipts: N=5, F=2, instance (0,0), one PUT command (key 1) and the NOOP the recovery generates.

The harness schedules delivery explicitly: the startRecoveryForInstance calls are the functions the executor invokes after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417), but no run() loop or executeCommands goroutine was active, and the crash points were chosen by the harness within the target's permitted failure model.

The completed contradiction required the executor's retry to be invoked a second time by the harness; the contradiction itself was measured, but the 10-second cadence and the executor's own decision to retry were modelled rather than run.

The premise that an accept broadcast reaches a replica that never pre-accepted uses the target's Alive mechanism between the pre-accept and accept broadcasts; a real connection loss was not exercised.
Incidental observation not used by the claim: the recovered committed instance in receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 carries Seq -1 at replicas 2, 3 and 4 although startPhase1 computed seq 0.
interpretations.joint_history: Indices 7-9, 11-14 and 16-23 belong to receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 (value-adoption run, instance (0,0)); indices 6, 10, 11, 16, 19, 21-27 and 29 belong to receipt d80cbfd9f9a547639811aeacb19c0a30 (committed-value run with the executor retry, same instance (0,0)); both receipts are cited in the executions map and each describes its own run, so no measurement is combined across executions.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: the status-guard mechanism is executed on the first recovery attempt - the recovering replica adopts the COMMITTED status of a peer's pre-accept reply, discards the remaining replies and stays undecided - and the executor's retry then proceeds because the local value-ballot token has moved, so the stall is per-attempt rather than permanent; the retry's completion is the value-adoption defect's contradiction. Evidence: receipt 9b8471479d484a12bdaf961653bbbe54 (first attempt) shows replica 2 holding (0,0) COMMITTED with cmd_op 1 (index 11), its prepare reply reporting that status with a command (index 16), the recovery nevertheless proposing the NOOP (index 19), and the recovering replica ending PREACCEPTED (index 21; comparison 1 of that experiment violated with witness 21) while the second acceptor had handled the PreAccept and replied (index 23). Receipt d80cbfd9f9a547639811aeacb19c0a30 measures the retry: the second attempt's prepare replies match its ballot (index 22 from replica 2 with Status COMMITTED, index 23 from replica 4), three replies are appended and the dispatch happens (index 24: instance status ACCEPTED), and the retry commits the NOOP (index 25: replica 3 COMMITTED with cmd_op 0; index 27: replica 4 the same) while replica 2 keeps X committed (index 26). The mechanism is sourced: the adoption block epaxos/epaxos.go:876-881 overwrites lb.status with a reply's COMMITTED status on the restarted phase-1 path, and the guard at epaxos/epaxos.go:870 then returns for every remaining reply carrying a matching ballot, so lb.preAcceptOKs stops at one and neither the fast nor the slow commit branch is entered on that attempt; on the next attempt the coordinator's own vbal token equals the tried ballot, so the COMMITTED reply is no longer adopted, the reply is counted, and sub-case 3 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1269-1272) leads to the accept phase that commits the NOOP.
counterevidence: The stall is per-attempt, not permanent: the measured retry dispatches and commits, so the mechanism delays the recovered proposal by one executor interval rather than blocking it forever.

The peer holding X is protected in its own state (epaxos/epaxos.go:1082), so the status-guard mechanism itself does not rewrite that replica; the contradiction arises from the recovery's own fabricated value.
The peer's COMMITTED status is the target's own honest answer; the defect lies in the recovering side's handling of that answer, not in the peer's reply.
limitations: One configuration and one instance (0,0) with N=5, F=2 and one command; the guard's interaction was not exercised for a leader that holds its own command, nor with a lower ballot on the COMMITTED reply.
The executor interval between attempts was not run: the harness invoked the second startRecoveryForInstance directly, so the 10-second delay itself is modelled.
The recovering replica's own instance reaches a decided state only after the retry, and dependents of (0,0) at that replica were not executed.
interpretations.joint_history: Indices 11, 16, 19, 20, 21 and 23 belong to receipt 9b8471479d484a12bdaf961653bbbe54 (first attempt) and indices 16, 19 and 21-27 belong to receipt d80cbfd9f9a547639811aeacb19c0a30 (retry attempt); both receipts are separate runs of the same instance (0,0) in the committed-value harness family, and the retry claim is grounded only in the later receipt.
